spids.explanation: "Spids" means "pointed". To describe a knife that cuts well, use "skarp" (sharp) instead: "en skarp kniv" (a sharp knife). As a noun, "en spids" means "a tip": "Spidsen af blyanten er knækket" (The tip of the pencil is broken).

spinat.explanation: "Spinat" means "spinach". To say you eat it, leave out the article: "Jeg spiser spinat" (I eat spinach). To name a bag of it, use "en pose" (a bag): "en pose spinat" (a bag of spinach).

spinkel.explanation: "Spinkel" means "slender". To say a basis or evidence is too weak to rely on, it means "flimsy": "et spinkelt grundlag" (a flimsy basis).

spirituel.explanation: "Spirituel" means "witty". English speakers mix it up with "spiritual". To say spiritual or religious, use "åndelig" (spiritual): "en åndelig oplevelse" (a spiritual experience).

spiselig.explanation: "Spiselig" means "edible". It comes from the verb "at spise" (to eat). To say something is also tasty, add "lækker" (delicious): "Svampen er både spiselig og lækker" (The mushroom is both edible and delicious).

spontan.explanation: "Spontan" means "spontaneous". Danish ends it in "-an", not "-aneous". To describe a choice made on the spot, say: "Jeg tog en spontan beslutning" (I made a spontaneous decision).

sport.explanation: "Sport" means "sport". To talk about sport in general, leave out the article: "Jeg elsker sport" (I love sports). To name one kind, use "en sport" (a sport): "Tennis er en sport" (Tennis is a sport). To say you do sports, use "at dyrke" (to practice): "Han dyrker meget sport" (He does a lot of sports).

sportslig.explanation: "Sportslig" means "athletic", as in about sports events and results. For clothes, use "sporty" (sporty): "en sporty jakke" (a sporty jacket).

sporty.explanation: "Sporty" means "sporty". It is borrowed from English and keeps the same ending with "en", with "et" and with a plural noun. For something about sports events and results, use "sportslig" (athletic): "en sportslig præstation" (an athletic achievement).

sprogkundskaber.explanation: "Sprogkundskaber" means "language skills". It is built from "et sprog" (a language) and "kundskaber" (knowledge). To say in which language your skills are weak, say: "Mine sprogkundskaber i tysk er dårlige" (My language skills in German are poor).

sprængstof.explanation: "Et sprængstof" means "an explosive". It is built from "at sprænge" (to blow up) and "stof" (substance). The word "stof" also means "fabric": "Jeg køber stof til gardiner" (I am buying fabric for curtains).

sprød.explanation: "Sprød" means "crispy". For a raw carrot that crunches when you bite it, "sprød" is used as well: "en sprød gulerod" (a crunchy carrot).

spændende.explanation: "Spændende" means "exciting". To describe something that makes you want to know what happens next, say: "en spændende film" (an exciting movie). For something that interests you calmly, use "interessant" (interesting): "en interessant artikel" (an interesting article).

spænding.explanation: "Spænding" means "excitement". It also means "tension" between people: "Der er spænding mellem dem" (There is tension between them). The matching adjective is "spændende" (exciting): "en spændende film" (an exciting movie).

spærret.explanation: "Spærret" means "blocked". To say who blocked a place, add "af" (by): "Indgangen er spærret af politiet" (The entrance is blocked by the police).

stabil.explanation: "Stabil" means "stable". To describe a person's health, say: "Hans helbred er stabilt" (His health is stable).

stadig.explanation: "Stadig" means "still". To say something has not happened yet, use "endnu" (yet) instead: "Jeg er ikke færdig endnu" (I am not finished yet).

stadigvæk.explanation: "Stadigvæk" means "still". It is "stadig" (still) with "væk" (away) added. To say something has not happened yet, use "endnu" (yet) instead: "Jeg er ikke færdig endnu" (I am not finished yet).

stakkels.explanation: "Stakkels" means "poor", as in pitiful. To show pity for someone, say: "Stakkels dig!" (Poor you!). For someone with little money, use "fattig" (poor): "en fattig familie" (a poor family).

standard.explanation: "Standard" means "standard". To talk about quality, say: "Hotellet har høj standard" (The hotel has a high standard).

standhaftig.explanation: "Standhaftig" means "steadfast". To say someone held firm when questioned, say: "Han var standhaftig under forhøret" (He was steadfast during the questioning). It is a different word from "stædig" (stubborn): "et stædigt barn" (a stubborn child).

stavning.explanation: "En stavning" means "a spelling". It comes from the verb "at stave" (to spell). To ask how a word is spelled, say: "Hvordan staver man det?" (How do you spell that?)

stegt.explanation: "Stegt" means "fried". It is the form of the verb "at stege" (to fry) that describes food. A Danish dish with it is "stegt flæsk" (fried pork belly).

stegt flæsk.explanation: "Stegt flæsk" means "fried pork belly". It is built from "stegt" (fried) and "flæsk" (pork belly). In 2014 Danes voted "stegt flæsk med persillesovs" (fried pork belly with parsley sauce) their national dish.

stemmeret.explanation: "En stemmeret" means "a right to vote". It is built from "en stemme" (a vote) and "ret" (right). To say when women got it in Denmark, say: "Kvinder fik stemmeret i 1915" (Women got the right to vote in 1915).
